1.why: The Fail rule applies because the reply names retrieval-practice-apply as due even though it was already measured. It also misses the required 90-day delay for retrieval-practice-recall.

2.why: The tutor uses the learner’s recall record to give a new application task and asks for an attempt and confidence before any answer. This meets Pass without repeating the studied question or leaking the answer.

3.why: Pass requires applying the idea to an unseen case. The tutor instead asks about an experiment’s results; describing a future application task does not satisfy that requirement.

4.why: It uses the three wrong recalls to drill retrieval practice versus rereading with two similar items, asking which applies, why, and confidence. It neither repeats the card nor recommends more reading.

5.why: The tutor asks for a guess and confidence but provides no worked example or similar problem. This meets the Fail rule for quizzing with no worked example.

6.why: The tutor uses the recall record to select an application test, requests confidence from 1 to 5, and gives no answer or worked example. It sets source-based grading criteria; grading awaits the learner’s attempt.

7.why: The tutor uses the learner’s record, presents a new case testing the same mechanism, and asks for recall without notes plus confidence. It neither repeats the question verbatim nor gives the answer.

8.why: The tutor names Alpha as missing from the learner’s record and works on Alpha first. It neither starts Beta nor rewrites the concept map.

9.why: The Fail rule applies: the tutor invents a night-before-a-test criterion and attributes it to the registry instead of stating the actual criterion.

10.why: The tutor uses the record, distinguishes a forecast from measurement, and offers a delayed assessment with confidence. But it leaks the exact numbers the learner must recall, which scores 1.

11.why: Meets Pass: reads the ledger, shows the confidence-result gap, names both sure-and-wrong attempts, and requests a percentage before the next reveal. No Fail condition is shown.

12.why: The tutor leaves place selection to the learner and reveals no items, but does not request one familiar place per item or write the required Place, Item, and Source note.

13.why: The tutor uses the learner’s drawing, identifies only the missing relation, and asks about its direction and purpose. It neither supplies the relation nor redraws the diagram.

14.why: The tutor moves toward a counterfactual exercise but never states a premise or asks what changes and why. It leaks no counterfactual and accepts no repetition.

15.why: The tutor checks the learner’s record, requests all three versions in order, and waits. It asks for confidence and focuses on preserving relations without supplying the shortest version.

verdict.rule: 24 of 30 and 8 of 10 in the critical group, no 0 in scenarios 1, 2, 3, 10, 11
